blocks.text: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are usually caused by bacteria, most commonly Escherichia coli. The bacteria enter the urinary system through the urethra and infect the bladder, the ureters or the kidneys.

blocks.caption: A urinary tract infection
rows: bacteria, most often Escherichia coli, entering through the urethra
frequent and urgent need to urinate; pain or burning on urination; cloudy or strong-smelling urine; lower abdominal pain; sometimes fever or chills
a course of antibiotics to kill the bacteria; drinking plenty of water and urinating often help flush them out and ease the symptoms

blocks.prompt: Why does drinking plenty of water help in a UTI?
blocks.explanation: More water means more urine and more frequent urination, which flushes bacteria out of the urinary tract, alongside the antibiotics.

items: UTI: bacteria (mostly E. coli) via the urethra; urgency, burning, cloudy urine; antibiotics and plenty of water.
